correct_completion: I used to play in the garden every afternoon.
full_sentence: When I was a child, I used to play in the garden every afternoon.
acceptable_variants: I would play in the garden every afternoon.
I often played in the garden after school.

options.text: I am playing in the garden now.
options.why_wrong: The present continuous describes an action happening now. The stem refers to a past habit, so a past form is needed.

options.text: I have played in the garden for years.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect connects the past to the present. The stem describes a finished period of childhood, so 'used to' fits better.

options.text: I used to play in the garden every afternoon.
I will play in the garden tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense refers to a time after now. The stem is about a past habit, so this does not fit.

grammar_focus: Used to for past habits and states that no longer happen
explanation: The stem sets up a childhood time frame, so the completion must describe a repeated past habit. 'Used to' expresses this, and it signals that the habit has stopped. Turkish speakers often use a simple past here because Turkish marks habitual past with a suffix rather than a separate phrase.
